title: Non-grey dust at 1841 K passes a representative three-band CPV infrared test
abstract: We test whether a blackbody infrared limit also applies to non-grey absorbing dust. We solve finite-star radiative equilibrium with the same wavelength-dependent efficiency for heating and emission. We compare exact thermal colour ratios with the released Ks/W1, W2/W1 and W3/W1 signal and bootstrap covariance for 78 young CPV hosts. For a representative 3200 K star at 1.95 stellar radii, an absorption exponent of 0.79 gives dust at 1841 K. At the source summed-depth optical-area scale, the squared joint distance is 4.24, below the nominal 95% threshold of 7.81. The null gives 4.31 and grey grains in this representative model give 115. The same fixed model also passes a four-band test with Gaia RP as the reference (6.78 versus 9.49). These tests are not independent. Non-grey emission reverses the W3/W1 colour change. Thus a temperature ceiling below 2000 K does not by itself extend the blackbody test to absorbing dust. This is a conditional model counterexample, not a population dust fit or detection. Blackbody stellar spectra, effective wavelengths, a phenomenological efficiency and non-simultaneous source data limit the result. We include a 4920-case grid, independent analytic checks, original code and exact input hashes.

display.caption: Coupled equilibrium temperature, infrared colour and joint distance in a representative star. Non-grey emission can reverse the W3/W1 signal. This is not a population fit.
